top_story_title: Actively exploited Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw added to CISA KEV
top_story_summary: CISA added two critical vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog citing reports of active exploitation in the wild. One of them is in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), the management plane of the VeloCloud SD-WAN estate. The other, CVE-2026-110447 (CVSS 9.2), is an OS command injection flaw in the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server used within NextCloud - not network infrastructure, but it arrived in the same KEV batch and will appear on the same compliance report. The report naming both entries does not state the CVE ID, affected releases or fixed build for the Arista flaw, so take those from Arista's own advisory and the KEV catalog entry rather than from secondary coverage.
top_actions: Inventory every Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator instance and its running version; pull the CVE ID and fixed release from Arista's advisory and the KEV entry - this report does not state them, so check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
Remove VCO web UI and API access from the internet now: bind management to a management network or jump host and enforce an explicit source ACL at the perimeter.
Patch the orchestrator before the edge devices, then validate certificate trust and config sync across the fabric after the upgrade.
Rotate orchestrator admin credentials, API tokens and edge activation keys after patching, not before; enforce MFA on every orchestrator admin account and remove shared local admins.
Diff edge templates, profiles and policy objects against a known-good export, looking for overrides, routes or tunnel changes nobody filed a ticket for.
executive_summary: CISA added an actively exploited Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator vulnerability to KEV; the SD-WAN management plane can push config to every edge device, so treat it as fleet-wide. The CVE and fixed release are not in the report - take them from Arista's advisory.

A large-scale campaign against internet-exposed Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect devices has exposed more than 70,000 credentials, with attempted follow-on compromise of victim organisations. Rotate VPN and admin credentials and assume stolen sessions.

HPE patched 72 ArubaOS vulnerabilities including eight maximum-severity authentication bypass and remote code execution flaws. No CVEs or fixed builds in the source - read them off the HPE advisory before planning the controller upgrade.

Two critical PHP RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, dubbed PHP2shell) are now being tracked by both Cisco and Palo Alto Networks PSIRT against their product lines. Watch both advisories for the affected-product tables.
Cisco issued an emergency informational advisory on distrusting eight eMudhra intermediate CAs whose private keys are brute-forceable in seconds - a trust-store action, not a patch.

Dropped as out of scope this cycle: a Windows UEFI bootkit, an abandoned media-player updater, a developer-focused infostealer, a Microsoft AI-agent governance story and a vendor education announcement.
key_actions: **Arista** — Identify every VCO instance from the asset inventory, filtered by model and running version, and confirm it against Arista's fixed-release table.
**Arista** — Patch the orchestrator/controller before edge devices and validate certificate trust after the upgrade.

**Multiple** — Treat this as a credential incident first: force a password reset for all VPN users and rotate every local admin credential, API key, certificate and VPN pre-shared key on the affected gateways.
**Multiple** — Terminate all active VPN sessions and revoke session tokens; assume stolen session cookies remain valid until explicitly invalidated.
**HPE Aruba** — Map ArubaOS versions across all controllers and APs and compare them against HPE's fixed-release table; the specific builds are in the advisory, not in this report.
**HPE Aruba** — Patch controllers first, then stage the AP upgrade behind them.
**Cisco** — Read the affected-product list in cisco-sa-emudhra-info-ScS22A1r and re-check it later, since Cisco states the advisory will be updated as information becomes available.

**Cisco** — Inventory where the eight eMudhra intermediates and their roots appear in device trust stores: VPN peer validation, 802.1X/RADIUS, management TLS, captive portals and any TLS-inspection CA bundle.

headlines.title: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Critical Flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud
headlines.summary: CISA added an actively exploited Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw to KEV, putting the SD-WAN management plane that configures every edge device under live attack.

headlines.title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials
headlines.summary: A mass campaign against exposed Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect edge devices has harvested over 70,000 credentials, with follow-on intrusion attempts.

headlines.title: HPE patches eight max severity RCE and auth bypass AOS flaws
headlines.summary: HPE patched 72 ArubaOS vulnerabilities, eight of them maximum-severity authentication bypass and remote code execution flaws in the wireless controller OS.

headlines.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
headlines.summary: Cisco issued an emergency informational advisory to distrust eight eMudhra intermediate CAs after a researcher showed their private keys can be brute-forced in seconds.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in PHP Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco is assessing its product line against two critical PHP remote code execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, being tracked as PHP2shell.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: HIGH)
headlines.summary: Palo Alto Networks rates the impact of the critical PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on its products as HIGH in a PSIRT advisory.
